title: Temporal trends in the incidence of chronic kidney disease from 1992 to 2021: An age-period-cohort analysis using GBD 2021 data and projections until 2031
content:
by Yu Zheng, Muhong Wei, Daibing Lu, Yuxin Liu, Xue Chen, Jing Mi, Wenjia Peng, Yuyuan Zhang

Background

This study analyzed the temporal trends in the incidence of Chronic kidney disease (CKD) globally and across various regions over the past 30 years, as well as projected incidence for the next 10 years. These findings may help identify regions and age groups where intensified CKD surveillance, prevention, and health-system planning should be prioritized.

Methods

Data on the number of CKD cases and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR) were obtained from the GBD 2021 dataset. The age, period, and cohort effects were assessed using the age-period-cohort (APC) model. Subsequently, a univariate autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model was developed based on the historical incidence time series to forecast incidence trends up to the year 2031.

Results

Globally, CKD incident cases rose from 8.24 million in 1992 to 19.94 million in 2021, representing a 141.99% increase (2.42-fold growth). The ASIR increased from 194.74 to 233.56 per 100,000, with an annual net drift of 0.79%. Among the different socio-demographic index (SDI) regions, net drift was lowest in high SDI regions(0.34% per year) and highest in middle SDI regions(1.06% per year). Age, period, and cohort effects demonstrated similar trends globally and across SDI regions: CKD risk increased with age, period and birth cohort. The ARIMA model projected global ASIR to reach 237.91 (95% CI: 227.54–248.28) per 100,000 by 2031. Except for a slight decrease in the high SDI region, an increasing trend was observed in the other four SDI regions.

Conclusion

This study suggests that the burden of CKD incidence increased over the past 30 years and could continue to rise in the coming decade. The middle SDI regions may warrant particular concern.
